Blizzard has called it "the biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players." Even though Grand Theft Auto 6 will be taking over the world tomorrow, World of Warcraft: Forever was the first game this month that people flocked to in record-breaking numbers. While we don't know the exact player count like we do with games on Steam, we can make an educated guess on just how many people dove into the MMO via a recent set of statistics from Blizzard. According to the official WoW X account, over 15 million characters were created in the last few weeks. Characters aren't individual players. You can create dozens of characters on your account if you want to, but I'd guess most people didn't do that. This is a game where you can put hundreds of hours into one character before ever reaching the level cap. There definitely aren't 15 million total players based on this statistic, but the number might not be massively below that. I can't say I'm surprised that a spin-off MMO that will remain stuck in the most universally nostalgic era of WoW was a big hit. Everyone who stopped playing for one reason or another came back to remember what it was like to smack a scorpion for 38 seconds. Whether or not they'll stick around is the question. Blizzard plans on updating the game with new things to do for players at different stages of the long leveling journey. Most people are still weeks away from reaching the level 60 cap, partially because there are so many things to do that don't involve XP. The first raid is around the corner, but I'm curious to see what kind of stuff is added for those of us who are still chilling in the mid-30s. titre: World of Warcraft Forever Officially Hits Player Peak it Hasn't Seen in 15 Years
chapo: World of Warcraft Forever breaks records with most players for Blizzard’s MMO in 15 years
extrait: The last time this many people were playing WoW, GTA 5 wasn't even out It was already clear that World of Warcraft: Forever, Blizzard's reimagining of the early days of the MMO, was a smash hit. During early access, before the game's full release, it brought back plenty of lapsed players and garnered praise. Now, with the dust having settled slightly two weeks after release, it is becoming clear that Forever is returning World of Warcraft to a level of popularity it hasn't seen in years. To celebrate Forever's continued success, the official World of Warcraft X account shared a handful of fun statistics ranging from how many characters and guilds have been created to how many times players have died. But it's a statistic shared by Holly Longdale, the game's executive producer and vice president, that really puts things into perspective. According to Longdale, World of Warcraft has more weekly players than at any point in the past 15 years thanks to Forever. That means the last time this many people were playing World of Warcraft, Cataclysm was the game's most recent expansion. That last popularity spike was also closer to the actual release of the MMO in 2004 than it is to Forever's release this year. Even World of Warcraft Classic, Blizzard's playable trip down memory lane, failed to ignite this much interest after launching in 2019.​​​​​​​ While Longdale's reveal is perhaps the most noteworthy​​​​​​​, there are some cool tidbits in the statistics Blizzard posted about Forever's first two weeks. Over 15 million characters have been created, and they've died nearly 200 million times in total​​​​​​​. That would average out to just over 13 deaths per character. Nearly 30 million deaths were due to PvP kills, though the deadliest boss in the game is Shadowfang Keep's​​​​​​​ Archmage Arugal. Forever is still fresh, though, and only time will tell if Blizzard can keep the game's momentum going as the weeks go on. The developer has consistently updated and tweaked​​​​​​​ the game to better address fan feedback and pain points. What would also be interesting to know is whether​​​​​​​ Forever has brought enough lapsed players back into the fold for them to return to the MMO's main retail version as well​​​​​​​. When the game's next expansion, The Last Titan, releases next year, perhaps​​​​​​​ the game will see a markedly​​​​​​​ larger player count​​​​​​​ as well.

chapo: Who have defeated nearly 10 billion enemies so far…

World of Warcraft: Forever is smashing records for Blizzard left, right, and center, it seems, having boasted the biggest concurrent player launch in the MMO's history – and now, more players engaging weekly than Azeroth has seen in over two decades. A good 15 years, to be precise, as World of Warcraft executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale reveals in a new post over on Twitter, celebrating one very impressive milestone from Forever: over 15 million characters logged so far. "Another fun statistic for you," the lead exclaims. "WoW: Forever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years. Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth." That's impressive, to say the least. Attached to her thread is a full look at the stats, too, and they're something all right. First, as Longdale notes, there are loads of players – 15,160,147, as of last night. Then, there's the number of quests that folks have completed: 1,480,343,357. Yes, nearly one and a half billion quests, y'all… and a whopping 9,786,925,806 (yep, that's over 9.7 billion) enemies defeated to boot. Holy moly. The hype train continues 🚊 You’re breaking records by the day! Thank you all for helping to create this amazing community. https://t.co/9EAkCbRzYUNovember 18, 2026 Through it all, players are managing to stay social as well, maintaining the heart of the MMO genre and what have you. A nice 140,764 guilds are up and running in Azeroth – but there's more. Fans have formed 71,309,889 parties together thus far, taking on World of Warcraft: Forever's more formidable foes and dungeons alongside pals. PvP is thriving, too (which comes as little surprise, considering the population fiasco Blizzard's worked to address). There have been almost 29 million PvP kills, 28,938,569 to be exact, with 196,851,761 player deaths in total. The numbers just keep on coming, eh? Something tells me they'll only grow from here as well, considering how steady WoW: Forever's popularity is proving.
